chunks: And with this chain, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Nasr ibn Muzahim, from Umar ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn al-Khalil, from Ya'qub ibn Sulayman, who said:

I and a group of people stayed awake one night, and we discussed the martyrdom of al-Husayn (peace be upon him). A man from the group said, 'No one who took part in his killing escaped without a calamity befalling his family, wealth, and self.' An old man from the group said, 'By Allah, I am among those who witnessed his killing and assisted in it, yet no disliked thing has befallen me until now.' The people disliked this (his claim), and the lamp changed (its flame), for its oil was naphtha. He went to it to fix it, and the fire caught his finger. He blew on it, and it caught his beard. He rushed to the water and threw himself into the river, but the fire continued to flutter on his head. When they took him out, it burned him until he died. May Allah curse him.
ai.seo_question: What is the story of the man who killed Imam Husain (a.s.) and his subsequent death by fire?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this incident in *Thawab al-A'mal* to illustrate the concept of *Barzakh* (intermediate state) punishment, where the old man’s body remained alive and conscious in the grave-like state of the lamp's fire. This narrative serves as a tangible sign (*Ayah*) for the companions, emphasizing that the curse of Allah upon the killers of Imam Husayn (a.s.) manifests in immediate, physical calamities affecting their very essence.
